decision: Use `pldg-20260624-001-provider-updates` as the active v2 Bootstrap Planning Ledger for the exact placeholder feature token `<provider updates>`. The ledger is source/planning memory only; canonical Plans and generated governance/build artifacts remain untouched until explicit compile, index, or governance-seal permission is given.
title: Initialize active feature planning ledger

decision: Treat `<provider updates>` as a provider-currentness ledger whose first design lane is replacing/updating old Gemini CLI provider assumptions with Antigravity CLI (`agy`) evidence before any canonical Plans edits.
title: Start provider update lane with Antigravity CLI

decision: Keep the Antigravity CLI work ledger-only until Jared explicitly asks to compile; current work may inspect live sources and existing Plans, but it must not modify canonical Plans, PlanUnit index, WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, Spec Lock, shards, evidence, plan_graph, or auto_decisions.
title: Keep Antigravity provider update ledger-only before compile

decision: Kill Gemini CLI support in PM and replace the stale Gemini CLI provider path with Antigravity CLI; do not preserve Gemini CLI as an active enterprise/API-key compatibility path in canonical product behavior.
title: Retire Gemini CLI as active PM provider support

decision: Model provider catalogs as `Provider -> models`, like OpenCode: each provider exposes its own supported model list and the same underlying model may appear under multiple providers without being globally deduplicated away from provider-specific auth, billing, quota, permissions, or capability evidence.
title: Use provider-to-model catalog structure

decision: Make thinking effort level selection a cross-provider and cross-model runtime/control concept, with requested/effective support-state disclosure rather than treating it as a provider-specific special case.
title: Make thinking effort a universal provider/model control

decision: Use local Antigravity CLI verification as ledger evidence: `agy` 1.0.11 installs and exposes the documented top-level commands, but authenticated model listing and prompt execution remain unverified because they require sign-in.
title: Record verified Antigravity CLI command surface with auth boundary

decision: Keep Gemini Direct API as an allowed direct provider path while retiring/removing Gemini CLI support and stale Gemini CLI helper/media assumptions from active PM provider behavior.
title: Keep Gemini Direct API while removing Gemini CLI

decision: Reframe media support as a provider/model capability matrix rather than a Gemini-default route: each provider/model route carries its own media-kind support, account/auth/quota constraints, endpoint parameters, and supported/unsupported/unknown verification state.
title: Reframe media support as provider/model capability matrix

decision: Add OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex image-generation currentness work to the provider update lane, using official OpenAI sources for ChatGPT Images 2.0, GPT Image 2/`gpt-image-2`, Codex `$imagegen`, API image routes, provenance, rate limits, and organization-verification constraints before compile.
title: Add OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex GPT Image 2 media lane

decision: Expand the media-support research scope across provider/model routes to include other media beyond image generation, specifically video, TTS/audio, and music, with explicit per-media support-state labels before any canonical Plans compile.
title: Research provider support across image, video, TTS/audio, and music

decision: Generalize the provider-family rule across vendors: PM should model separate provider entries by execution/auth/billing/control boundary, each with its own `Provider -> models` catalog, while user-facing surfaces may group related entries under a provider-family/vendor label such as OpenAI, Google, MiniMax, Z.AI, Alibaba, or similar families.
title: Apply provider-family grouping rule to all vendors

decision: Support both coding-plan provider products and separate general media API provider routes when both exist. Coding-plan providers stay coding-scoped unless they directly expose media, while general media API routes get independent auth, billing, quota, region, model, and media-capability records.
title: Support both coding-plan and general media API routes

decision: Close the verification threshold as no-uncertainty: canonical provider support claims require local proof of expected behavior or an explicit unsupported/blocked/removed disposition. Source docs and repo inspection can seed the matrix but must not leave active support behavior unresolved.
title: Require no-uncertainty provider verification before compile

decision: Use the pulled active OpenCode repository as direct-provider source-lineage/reference evidence for provider-owned model catalogs, modalities, provider/model API overrides, generated variants, and provider-specific thinking/reasoning wire mappings, with source pinned to commit `bcff162c60772aeccc8c6bbcf229da406a07eae5`.
title: Use pinned OpenCode repo inspection for direct-provider catalog reference

decision: CLI providers must be tested locally by the assistant before active support is compiled. Initial sanitized probes show multiple CLI routes are auth-gated, failing, unavailable, not installed, or explicitly removed, so compile must carry a verification matrix and blockers rather than unknown support states.
title: Require local CLI provider probe matrix

decision: Classify Codex and OpenCode as direct providers for this feature. Core PM support for those provider routes should not depend on bridging their CLIs; their CLI behavior is optional tooling evidence unless Jared later explicitly widens scope to CLI automation for them.
title: Treat Codex and OpenCode as direct providers rather than required CLI bridges

decision: Narrow the open CLI verification blocker to active CLI-bridged provider routes only: Antigravity CLI, Cursor Agent, Claude Code, and GitHub Copilot CLI through `gh`. Gemini CLI is removed/retired; Codex and OpenCode are direct-provider routes and are not active CLI blocker items.
title: Narrow active CLI bridge blocker scope

decision: Refine GitHub Copilot CLI support evidence against current `@github/copilot@1.0.65`: hosted Copilot prompt execution is blocked by explicit policy/subscription/license/admin enablement denial, while the current command surface includes reasoning effort, output-format, mode, attachment, and BYOK/custom-provider controls. Do not compile hosted Copilot CLI as working until a minimal prompt succeeds or the route is explicitly compiled as blocked/auth-gated.
title: Refine GitHub Copilot CLI blocker and current command surface

decision: Prefer a Cursor SDK / local OpenAI-compatible provider route as the primary Cursor support candidate, using `standardagents/composer-api` style behavior as source-lineage evidence, while keeping `cursor-agent` as a separate optional CLI-bridged route. The SDK/local API route still requires real local proof with a Cursor API key or running local API app before it can compile as supported.
title: Prefer Cursor SDK/local API route over direct Cursor Agent CLI bridging

decision: After local Cursor approach testing, keep `standardagents/composer-api` / Cursor SDK local API as the preferred primary Cursor support candidate, but compile Cursor support with separate verification states: setup/catalog verified, adapter/local-bridge verified, and live-provider completion verified. Raw `cursor-agent` and `opencode-cursor` remain blocked for live prompts in this environment; `composer-api` has passing adapter tests and SDK bridge validation but still lacks live completion proof without a real Cursor API key or running local app session.
title: Classify Cursor routes by setup, adapter, and live-completion verification

decision: Classify Cursor authentication by route. PM must treat Cursor app / interactive Cursor Agent CLI as browser-login/OAuth-style session auth; Cursor Agent headless scripting as API-key-capable through `--api-key` or `CURSOR_API_KEY`; Cursor SDK, Cursor REST/API, Cloud Agents, and `composer-api` local OpenAI-compatible bridge routes as API-key-authenticated; and `opencode-cursor` as hybrid/source-lineage evidence. This clarifies, but does not close, the current Cursor live-completion blockers.
title: Clarify Cursor auth as route-specific

decision: Set the Cursor OAuth/browser-login/session method as the primary Cursor support focus. PM should verify and later compile the Cursor app / interactive Cursor Agent CLI logged-in-session route first; SDK/API-key/local OpenAI-compatible bridge work is secondary, fallback, or source-lineage unless Jared explicitly promotes it. API-key proof must not be required as the main condition for OAuth-route support, and OAuth-route support must not be claimed until a minimal prompt works through the logged-in Cursor session.
title: Focus Cursor support on OAuth/session route

decision: Promote the direct Cursor Agent OAuth/session route from blocked to locally live-verified: browser login, status/about, 139-model catalog, text prompt, and stream-json prompt all succeeded without `CURSOR_API_KEY`. Keep `opencode-cursor` blocked/secondary because it still falls back to 14 models, fails under isolated HOME, and hangs when run against the real OAuth session.
title: Verify direct Cursor OAuth route and keep opencode-cursor blocked

decision: Promote Claude Code first-party `claude.ai` session route from blocked to locally live-verified for non-interactive provider use. JSON prompt, stream-json prompt with required `--verbose`, and `--effort low|medium|high` all succeeded on `sonnet` / `claude-sonnet-4-6`. Keep `claude doctor` out of the automation readiness gate because it fails with an Ink raw-mode error in this execution context.
title: Verify Claude Code first-party session route and effort selector

decision: Promote Antigravity CLI from auth-gated/blocker status to locally live-verified for the signed-in `agy` 1.0.12 route. Fresh Claude Code and Cursor Agent retests also confirm their already-verified logged-in session routes remain working. Thinking effort must stay provider/model-specific: Claude exposes `--effort`, Cursor exposes effort through parameterized model syntax and model variants, and Antigravity exposes effort in provider model names.
title: Promote Antigravity and retest logged-in Claude/Cursor routes

decision: Treat the OpenCode server API as the direct-provider integration surface for OpenCode: `opencode serve` 1.17.11 exposes health, OpenAPI, provider/model catalogs, media capability metadata, and successful HTTP prompt execution through `opencode/big-pickle`. Keep OpenCode-server-routed GitHub Copilot separate and blocked because its live prompt returned no text and server logs showed `AI_APICallError: Forbidden`.
title: Use OpenCode server as direct provider and block server-routed Copilot

decision: Lock Cursor support planning to the direct Cursor Agent OAuth/browser-login/session route for the primary implementation. The compile plan should use local `cursor-agent` for auth/status, model discovery, prompt execution, output parsing, and effort/model selection. Keep `opencode-cursor` blocked/secondary and Cursor SDK/API/composer-api/local bridge work secondary/fallback/source-lineage unless Jared explicitly promotes those routes.
title: Lock Cursor primary implementation route

decision: Revise Cursor planning away from a final lock on plain `cursor-agent --print`. Treat `composer-api` local macOS OpenAI-compatible HTTP server as the preferred direct-provider candidate if it passes live local verification with a Cursor Dashboard API key; treat Cursor ACP via `agent acp` as a verified first-party session/agent protocol; keep `cursor-agent --print` as a verified fallback CLI bridge; keep `opencode-cursor` blocked/non-primary.
title: Promote composer-api to preferred Cursor direct-provider candidate pending proof

decision: Promote Cursor native API-key / SDK / composer-api-style support from pending candidate to live-verified direct provider planning route. The provided Cursor API key was used only as a redacted live credential; direct `@cursor/sdk`, composer-api Responses proxy, local-agent bridge, and temp Worker `/v1` surface all returned successful local completions. PM should not depend on `opencode-cursor`; OpenCode needs that plugin for Cursor, but PM has native support. Cursor ACP remains a verified first-party session/agent protocol, and plain `cursor-agent --print` remains a verified fallback CLI bridge.
title: Promote native Cursor API-key route after live verification

decision: Address the Claude Code `rate_limits` status-line change in PM provider planning. Claude Code usage/status integrations should prefer the local status-line stdin JSON fields `rate_limits.five_hour.*` and `rate_limits.seven_day.*` over OAuth usage endpoint polling, while gracefully handling missing fields and preserving `effort.level` and `thinking.enabled`.
title: Address Claude Code status-line rate limits in provider plans

decision: Treat coding plans as provider-specific first-class routes with live verification, not as a generic OpenAI provider bucket. Alibaba/Qwen Coding Plan gets a regioned/versioned provider setup; Kimi For Coding gets a provider-specific parity and client-identity risk lane; Z.AI/Zhipu, Tencent, MiniMax, KUAE, Umans, and related coding-plan products get explicit provider/model/media/thinking/verification records. OpenCode/Models.dev is source-lineage/catalog evidence, not sufficient support proof.
title: Treat coding plans as provider-specific first-class routes

decision: Use the current OpenCode repo as an implementation reference for first-class coding-plan provider architecture, but implement PM-owned provider/model transform mappings and tests. OpenCode confirms coding-plan products are first-class catalog/provider IDs through Models.dev and generic AI SDK packages, but it does not provide complete bespoke adapters and currently appears incomplete for Alibaba/Qwen Coding Plan `enable_thinking`. PM should copy the pattern, not the assumptions.
title: Use OpenCode as architecture reference, not complete coding-plan oracle

decision: Adopt only the provider-adjacent audit gaps not already covered by the active provider-update ledger. The ledger already covers Gemini CLI retirement/Antigravity replacement, Provider -> models taxonomy, Cursor native/API-key plus ACP/fallback route hierarchy, media matrix direction, OpenCode as direct provider/source-lineage, coding-plan provider expansion, thinking-effort support, and Claude Code status-line `rate_limits`. The remaining compile deltas are now captured as accepted atoms for provider launcher/setup-health metadata, caller-scoped capability schema, account-bound GUI selectors, requested/effective account identity, provider-native tool/secret mediation, runtime artifact schemas, provider usage source-confidence, and stale-anchor retirement.
title: Adopt only uncovered provider-audit deltas into the ledger
